newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner looking for earlier movie rights.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner looking for earlier movie rights.

text.p: Time Warner Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Gerald Levin said the company intends to aggressively compete with the networks for the rights to movie premiers, which would allow it to eventually command higher rates from advertisers.
Levin said cable television's increasing competitive edge against the networks has led Time Warner to go after those rights years earlier than usual for cable syndication.
It's made all the more possible after Time Warner's merger with Turner Broadcasting System, which included properties of advertising-supported cable networks.
"We're talking about a structural change in the business," Levin said in a briefing with reporters after the company released its first quarter results.

Time Warner has purchased the rights to more than 50 movies, some of which were produced by its Warner Bros and New Line movie-making divisions. But that package of films, also includes "The English Patient," which was released by Walt Disney Co's Miramax.
While movies usually premiere on broadcasting networks between three and five years after releases in the theaters, it normally takes a little over a decade before they appear in cable syndication.
As such, cable commands less money from advertisers for feature film premieres than the networks.

Levin said industry analysts believe the penetration rates of cable and broadcast will begin to intersect by 1998. But in some areas, particularly sports, cable has already surpassed broadcast, he said.
Time Warner cable channels now reach three out of four homes, he said.

Analysts said it is not an entirely new strategy on the part of Time Warner. However, with the increasing influence and presence of cable television in the home, it is more likely to occur, they said.
"They're identifying that as an opportunity to move the competition up a notch," A.G. Edwards analyst Michael Kupinski said.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk 212-859-1713))
